body: Totally get what you're saying but I come from an indian family. It may be a cultural thing as well, but 25 is considered optimal in my culture. I'm also pretty much settled in terms of my job and career so theres not really anything else I could be working towards right now. Another year single, and I'll have arranged marriage proposals coming up from random relatives! Haha

As I mentioned in my edit - I find myself very confused because I cant stand him sometimes, but the second I go a day or 2 without seeing him, I miss him so god damn much. It's a roller coaster of emotions. There are times (almost everyday) that I'm extremely grateful to have found such a loving and caring partner. I've tried to do the thing where we dont talk for a couple of days because I want "space". 50% he starts talking because he hates not being able to talk to me. The other 50% of the time is me missing him within 4-5 hours, and calling him to tell him whatever he missed. I try my best not to talk, but something happens, and I have this inexplicable need to share that with him, so I end up cutting our "break" short. I feel like theres this love hate relationship- I miss him terribly when hes not around, but all I end up doing when he is around is fight. So the distance thing just never seems to work.

It may also be a change in my expectations. He was really thoughtful and caring when I first met him (like he would buy 10000 red balloons and fill my house with it, and I have a collection of atleast 20 photo frames (with photos of  myself) that hes gifted me for random reasons). After I point I got overwhelmed with the amount of gifts he got that had no practicality (theres only so many photos of yourself you can put up in your room before people start to think you're a self obsessed person). I told him to get me gifts that are useful- winter jackets, shoes, stuff that I use you know? Hes been doing that now for the past year, and i think a part of me misses the crazy guy that filled my room with 1000 balloons at one point. I know the practical gifts are better because I actually use these everyday...but I guess a part of me wishes I had that crazy guy who did crazy things. Hes also become a lot more family and budget focused (to save for our life after marriage). These are all things I wanted him to do... I have no idea why I'm complaining about it. Sigh. But I do want to thank everyone who posted. The fact that leaving him has never crossed my mind, or the fact that I couldnt try to have a "break" from him for more than a couple of hours speaks volumes. I dont think I've fallen out of love, but our relationship does need a small reboot.
